rationale: ONTOLOGY (2026-10-03): the provide/inject CONTRACT edge is matched by NAME, and in JavaScript a name test also matches constructs that are not Vue's provide/inject. The DECORATOR shape produced a FABRICATED edge inside this lane's own fixtures: `@inject("db")` is a DI decorator whose argument is a string the component never receives, and the pre-fix analyzer published `references <Component> -> db` carrying `metadata.isInjectContract` at confidence 0.9. It was found by reading the output of `vue/decorator-metadata-868` — a fixture written for the #868 line-mirror seam, whose failure had nothing to do with it. Corpus incidence is 0 of the 79 contract calls on 1,151 admitted .vue files, so no sweep on this corpus could have surfaced it: that 0 is a LATENT defect, and the fixture is what makes it visible. `inject` is imported FROM 'vue' in this file, which isolates the decorator guard — an import from vue is the strongest evidence the name IS Vue's, so the local-shadow and foreign-import guards are both silent and only the decorator guard can be what rejects the row. The positives are here because a guard that stopped matching everything would pass a forbid-only fixture; the corpus writes 74 bare-global and 5 from-vue contract calls and both shapes are pinned across this file and `vue/contract-call-local-shadow`. The local-shadow partner cannot live in this file: it is the same call name in the same block, and pinning both would ask the analyzer to match and reject one identifier at once. The `Pool -> inject` row required below is the JS DELEGATE's decorator REFERENCE edge (`metadata.isDecorator`), a different relationship from the contract edge: it is pinned deliberately, because a 'fix' that suppressed `inject` under a decorator altogether would delete a correct edge while removing the fabricated one, and only requiring both makes the distinction checkable.
